reachable: Yes, at the scored position specifically, and the mechanism gets gradient. Structurally: with L odd the last command index is n_cmd-1 == n_pair, so the transport loop takes the obs_i = 0 / a_i = 0 branch there (no withheld observation is consulted), reads s_pre from memory written by strictly earlier steps, and that read flows through g_tr * tr_read(tr_reads) into pred_cmd at position L-1. Empirically, on a 13-token (odd) sequence with tr_read given nonzero weights to stand in for a trained readout, the prediction at the scored position moves when I disable the erase gate (delta 1.04e-3), flip the router role bias (1.68e-3), raise the codebook snap gate (0.204), or perturb a mid-chain mv command token (0.0875) — versus 1.127 for perturbing the read command itself. All three added mechanisms are live at the scored read. Gradient: the whole transport path is bottlenecked behind the zero-initialised tr_read readout (inherited from the parent), so on training step 1 every new parameter has exactly zero gradient; from step 2 onward all of them are nonzero (tr_route.weight 5.1e-5, tr_codes 2.6e-5, tr_snap_gate 6.2e-5, tr_erase.weight 4.5e-6, tr_slot_a 1.5e-4, tr_addr_in 2.7e-4) and growing as tr_read.weight grows (norm 0 -> 0.019 -> 0.056 over three steps). The erase gate is the weakest-gradient of the new parts by about an order of magnitude, so whether it learns anything inside the real step budget is an open empirical question, not a structural one. Causality re-checked on the transport loop directly: perturbing command step 4 leaves the transition reads at steps 0-3 bit-identical and changes only steps >= 4.
solves_outside_model: No. Nothing is resolved outside the model. The arch's only inputs are (tok_emb, types, key_pad); it never sees command strings, and a grep for split/startswith/re/str/'mv'/cmds over the file returns no string handling at all — the only hits are variable names like `before` and `obs_i`. cmd_raw is simply tok_emb[:, 0::2, :], the frozen standardized command embeddings the baseline already sees. The router, the four extractors, the codebook and the erase gate are all learned tensor maps of that embedding; no path is parsed, no move chain is resolved in Python, no routing table is built, and nothing is stamped into a token. This is not the retracted shape: the retracted stream resolved the chain and wrote the answer into the read token; here the read token is untouched (stream is baseline_interleave, unchanged from the parent) and the addresses are learned projections. The genome is identical to the parent's on every axis except arch, so no batcher/target/head loophole was opened either.
summary: The code does what the hypothesis says. The diff against the parent (r20_dualkey_contentgated_transition_worldmodel) is exactly the three advertised additions and nothing else: (1) a 4-slot address bank with a softmax role router whose input is only a GELU feature of the raw frozen command embedding, biased read->slot0 / write->slot1; (2) a shared learned codebook cleanup applied identically to both roles with a single gate at sigmoid(-2) = 0.119; (3) a destructive read that subtracts e * p_r (x) s_pre after the step's own read. Each was verified by execution rather than reading: the erase reproduces (1-e)*s_pre to 1e-6; the router and erase gate are exactly invariant to step position; the cleanup at init preserves address separation (cos 0.994 to the raw address, pairwise cosines essentially unchanged), and at g->1 with an untrained codebook it collapses to mean pairwise cos 0.65 — which is one of the failure modes the author explicitly listed, so the hypothesis is honest about its own risk. The four divergences I found are all wording, not mechanism: "p_r == p_w exactly at init" is really cos 0.9991 (random router weights break the symmetry through the untrained slots 2/3); "nothing I added is a function of the position index" is true of the router and the erase gate but the mixture is taken over the parent's position-carrying extractors, so the composite address is still mildly position-sensitive (inherited, not added); the "from the partner, kept verbatim" attribution is really "from the parent, unchanged"; and the "50% more work in that loop" figure is unprofiled and understates where the cost went (+18% forward wall-clock, +7.7% params). The hypothesis states no fabricated measured numbers — it explicitly labels everything UNMEASURED, which is the correct posture for a jail with no torch. The one thing worth flagging to whoever reads the archive entry: the mechanism's gradient is bottlenecked behind the parent's zero-initialised tr_read readout and starts at 1e-4-scale magnitudes, and the erase gate in particular is another order of magnitude weaker, so a null result here would not distinguish "the router cannot learn the verb-conditional role assignment" from "it never got enough signal to try".

divergences.claim: "The router bias is initialised so read role -> slot 0 and write role -> slot 1; since those two extractors are identical copies at init, p_r == p_w exactly at initialisation, which is the partner's single-slot read-modify-write as the starting point."
divergences.what_the_code_does: p_r and p_w are close but NOT equal at init. tr_route.weight is initialised normal(0, 0.02), so the read-role and write-role softmaxes put slightly different mass on the untrained, mutually different slots 2 and 3; those residues do not cancel even though s0 == s1. Measured over random inputs: cos(p_r, p_w) in [0.99906, 0.99999], max |p_r - p_w| = 1.4e-2. The substantive intent (start near single-slot read-modify-write) is preserved; the word "exactly" is wrong. Note also the init address is not the parent's p_r either: it is ~0.90*s0 + ~0.10 of two random directions, then blended 0.119 toward a random codebook direction.
divergences.evidence: Built the impl and called net._addresses on random (x_cmd, cmd_raw): 'init cos(p_r,p_w): min 0.999060 max 0.999989 / init max |p_r-p_w|: 1.402e-02'. Router weights at init: read [0.865, 0.034, 0.054, 0.048], write [0.043, 0.859, 0.053, 0.044]. tr_path_w.weight == tr_path.weight confirmed True.

divergences.claim: "nothing I added is a function of the position index or of the identity of the read location, which are identical in both arms and contribute exactly zero" / "the new machinery cannot express 'the content of whichever step moved first'"
divergences.what_the_code_does: The parts the author added — the router mixture weights, the erase gate, the codebook — are exactly position-invariant (verified: identical for the same command embedding placed at two different step indices). But the mixture is taken over slots 0 and 1, which are tr_path/tr_path_w applied to x_cmd, and x_cmd carries pos_scale * sinusoidal positional encoding. So the composite addresses p_r/p_w remain position-sensitive, and at init the router puts ~0.90 of its mass on exactly those two position-carrying extractors. No NEW position channel is introduced (this is the parent's channel, unchanged), but the claim as literally worded — that the added machinery cannot express a move-order-keyed lookup — overstates: it can multiplicatively modulate a position-dependent address. Only slots 2/3 are genuinely position-free.
divergences.evidence: Same 768-d command embedding placed at cmd steps 1 and 5 of a 13-token sequence: cos(s2_1, s2_5) = 1.0 exactly (position-free extractor), cos(s0_1, s0_5) = 0.99595 (parent's extractor, position-contaminated), cos(p_r_1, p_r_5) = 0.99614. Erase gate identical to full precision (0.09274658 both). pos_scale = 0.2, learnable.

divergences.claim: "From the partner: the shared latent-transition operator and its `transition_from_emb` entry point, kept verbatim so a head that supervises the operator as a forward model still reaches it."
divergences.what_the_code_does: Both methods are byte-identical to the PARENT's, not imported from the partner; and transition_from_emb in the partner (r18_pathstate_latent_transition_worldmodel) is NOT identical to the parent's version, so nothing was actually carried over from the partner's source. The crossover's only real debt to the partner is the conceptual single-slot read-modify-write starting point, which the parent already implements via the tr_path_w weight copy. The functional claim (a head supervising the operator still reaches it) is true: the head does getattr(net, 'transition_from_emb') and the method is present and unchanged.
divergences.evidence: Function-body comparison across the three files: _transition r18==r20 True, r20==candidate True; transition_from_emb r18==r20 False, r20==candidate True. Head r4_chainlink_route_transport line 404: op = getattr(net, "transition_from_emb", None).

divergences.claim: "The extra cost is one additional batched outer product per command step in the transport loop (about 50% more work in that loop, which is a small part of the forward) plus a few small projections; I have not profiled it."
divergences.what_the_code_does: Correctly declared unmeasured. The loop goes from 3 bmm to 4 bmm per step (+33%, not +50%), but the address computation outside the loop grew substantially: LayerNorm(768) + Linear(768->256) + four key projections + a 96-code softmax cleanup applied twice per step. Measured end-to-end forward on CPU at B=8, L=41: parent 28.8 ms vs candidate 34.1 ms (+18%); params 3,132,217 -> 3,371,845 (+7.7%).
divergences.evidence: Timed 5 forwards of each after a warm-up, same seed and same input tensors; parameter counts from sum(p.numel()).
